Add, remove and list the sections of a lab

Source: R/toolkit-lab.R
add_lab_section.Rd

add_lab_section() adds one of the ready-made sections in lab_section_types(). add_lab_exercise() adds a coding exercise you write yourself, and add_lab_question() a multiple-choice question. remove_lab_section() deletes a section and lab_outline() lists them.

Usage

add_lab_section(lab, type, after = NULL, id = NULL)

add_lab_exercise(
  lab,
  title,
  prompt,
  solution,
  starter = NULL,
  check = NULL,
  hint = NULL,
  use_fit = FALSE,
  after = NULL,
  id = NULL
)

add_lab_question(
  lab,
  question,
  answers,
  correct,
  messages = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  after = NULL,
  id = NULL
)

remove_lab_section(lab, id)

lab_outline(lab)

Arguments

lab

the lab folder (or its .Rmd file).

type

the kind of section; see lab_section_types().

after

the id of the section to put the new one after (see lab_outline()).

id

the new section's id, used in its chunk labels. Defaults to the type (for add_lab_section()) or a slug of the title, made unique.

title

the section heading.

prompt

the instructions students read, in Markdown (a character vector is joined with line breaks).

solution

R code that solves the exercise.

starter

R code students start from, for example with a blank to fill. Defaults to an empty exercise box.

check

R code that checks the student's result, run after their code. Use lab_need(condition, "message") to fail with a message, and .result for the value of the student's last line; the last value, if a string, is shown on success. Defaults to accepting any code that runs.

hint

optional hint (R code or comments).

use_fit

logical; start from the lab's fitted one-factor model fit (labs made with new_lab() only).

question

the question text.

answers

the answer options (character).

correct

which answers are correct: Their positions in answers, or the answers themselves. More than one makes a check-all-that-apply question.

messages

optional feedback for each answer, in the same order.

Value

lab_outline() returns a tibble with one row per section: id, type ("built-in" for unmarked sections), title, and the number of exercises and questions in it. The other functions return the .Rmd path, invisibly.

Details

Sections start with a level-2 heading (## ), marked by an <!-- mv-section: ... --> comment in labs made with the toolkit. These functions also work on copies of the built-in labs made with copy_lab(), whose sections are identified by their headings.

New content goes before the lab's "wrap-up" section if it has one, otherwise at the end, unless you name a section in after.

See also

new_lab(), check_material()

Examples

course <- file.path(tempdir(), "sections-demo")
lab <- new_lab("demo", data = expand.table(LSAT7), course = course,
               sections = c("intro", "wrap-up"))
add_lab_section(lab, "classical")
add_lab_exercise(lab, title = "Total scores",
  prompt = "Compute each person's total score and save it as `total`.",
  solution = "total <- rowSums(resp)",
  check = c("lab_need(exists('total'), 'Save the totals as `total`.')",
            "lab_need(length(total) == nrow(resp), 'One total per person.')",
            "'Well done.'"))
add_lab_question(lab, "What does a low item mean tell you?",
  answers = c("The item is hard", "The item is easy"), correct = 1)
lab_outline(lab)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   id                               type      title           exercises questions
#>   <chr>                            <chr>     <chr>               <int>     <int>
#> 1 intro                            intro     Meet the data           1         0
#> 2 classical                        classical Classical item…         2         1
#> 3 total-scores                     exercise  Total scores            1         0
#> 4 q-what-does-a-low-item-mean-tell question  Check your und…         0         1
#> 5 wrap-up                          wrap-up   Where to next           0         0
remove_lab_section(lab, "classical")
